title: is_rollback / crl_number_gt naming: both functions; one returns 'is this a rollback' the other 'is incoming greater'
description:
src/cache.rs:477-501: is_rollback and crl_number_gt have opposite semantic polarity — is_rollback returns true when the new entry is OLDER, crl_number_gt returns true when the incoming is NEWER. Reading the call site:

    if is_rollback(self.cache.get_crl(&key).as_deref(), meta.crl_number.as_deref()) { return; }

requires the reader to keep both inversions in head. is_rollback is the right verb for the caller's intent — flagging this as opinion only because the alternative (single comparator + clear ordering at the call site) sacrifices readability of the call site for symmetry of the helpers.

Skip if disagreeing. Marked opinion.
close_reason:
Not an opinion -- the parameter names were actively wrong at the only call site.

crl_number_gt was declared (incoming, stored) and returns first > second. Its sole caller, is_rollback, asks whether the number ALREADY CACHED exceeds the one arriving, so it calls crl_number_gt(prior_num, inc): 'prior' bound to a parameter named 'incoming', and 'incoming' bound to one named 'stored'. Both arguments bound to a parameter meaning the opposite of what was passed.

The behaviour was correct and the names were not, which is the worst combination available: the code worked, so nothing failed, and anyone editing that call site had to re-derive the polarity from the function body rather than trust the signature. The bead marked this 'opinion, skip if disagreeing'; it is a latent trap, not a preference.

Parameters are now positional (a_bytes, b_bytes) with the doc stating 'true iff a > b' and explaining why role names were removed, and the call site carries a comment naming the comparison it makes. Commit a829edc8.
